answer: A falcon tracing a comet follows a bright trail — our defense does the same with random walks launched from trusted seed agents across the interaction graph. Honest agents cluster densely through real work, while sybil identities sit in a sparse fringe, so walks rarely land on them. Each agent is scored by walk-landing probability; those at the nadir of trust may observe but cannot earn or vote until genuine collaboration pulls them into the core. Forging links to honest agents costs real interaction, so mass sybil creation stays uneconomical.
